verdict.rationale: First-party docs state Langfuse is open source under MIT. It can be self-hosted with Docker Compose, Kubernetes (Helm) or Terraform on AWS, Azure and GCP, runs the same infrastructure as Langfuse Cloud, and includes all core features for free without limitations. Community users confirm running it self-hosted and locally. Missing for 10: some enterprise features (RBAC roles, audit logs, data retention) need a license key, and users report a painful v2-to-v3 migration with extra dependencies (ClickHouse) for scalable self-hosting.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Langfuse is open source and can be self-hosted using Docker.
When self-hosting Langfuse, you run the same infrastructure that powers Langfuse Cloud.
Self-host all core Langfuse features for free without any limitations.
For production-scale deployments, we recommend one of the following options: Kubernetes (Helm), AWS (Terraform), Azure (Terraform), GCP (Terraform)
You can run Langfuse on a VM or locally using Docker Compose.
